title: Setting Up a Company in Türkiye as a Foreigner: LLC vs JSC Basics
seoTitle: Setting Up a Company in Türkiye as a Foreigner

quickAnswer: Foreigners can own 100% of a Turkish Limited Liability Company (Ltd. Şti.) or Joint Stock Company (A.Ş.), subject to TRY 50,000 or TRY 250,000 minimum capital respectively. Registration runs through MERSİS and the Trade Registry, while incorporation, tax, and compliance require a licensed Turkish attorney and certified public accountant (SMMM).

Can a foreigner own 100% of a Turkish Limited Company (Ltd. Şti.)?

Yes. Under the Turkish Commercial Code, foreign individuals and foreign corporate entities may own 100% of a Turkish Limited Liability Company (Limited Şirket, or Ltd. Şti.) or Joint Stock Company (Anonim Şirket, or A.Ş.) under the same establishment rules as domestic investors, with narrow exceptions in regulated sectors.

According to [Invest in Türkiye's Establishing a Business guide](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/establishing-a-business.aspx), nationality restrictions on shareholding and management apply only to specific sectors such as television broadcasting, maritime transport, and civil aviation. As confirmed by [CottGroup's 2026 minimum capital summary](https://www.cottgroup.com/tr/blog/item/deadline-for-joint-stock-and-limited-liability-companies-to-increase-their-capital-to-the-new-minimum-requirements-extended-to-december-31-2027), new formations require at least TRY 50,000 in capital for an LLC and TRY 250,000 for a standard JSC. Both structures allow a single shareholder, though a JSC offers cleaner share transfers and is preferred for institutional funding or joint ventures.

body.text: What steps require a Turkish tax number, notary and certified public accountant (SMMM)?

Every foreign shareholder and director needs a Turkish potential tax identity number before opening a blocked capital account or filing articles of association. Sworn translations and notarization of passports or foreign corporate resolutions are mandatory, and a licensed Serbest Muhasebeci Mali Müşavir (SMMM) must manage statutory bookkeeping and monthly tax filings.

Under [TÜRMOB's regulatory framework](https://www.turmob.org.tr/English), only licensed SMMMs may keep statutory books and file electronic tax returns. Your attorney and SMMM file Articles of Association via MERSİS, arrange sworn translations and notary attestations, pay the 0.04% Competition Authority fee, and issue the signature circular (imza sirküleri).
How long does company registration take in Istanbul?

Once translated, apostilled, and notarized documents are ready, the formal registration appointment at the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce (İTO) Trade Registry Directorate functions as a one-stop shop and typically completes within one to three business days. Allow two to three weeks end-to-end for document prep, tax inspection, and bank onboarding.

Per [Istanbul Chamber of Commerce (İTO)](https://www.ito.org.tr/en/services/trade-registry-procedures/establishment-procedure-of-limited-liability-companies) and [Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/establishing-a-business.aspx), the Trade Registry automatically notifies the tax office and SGK, publishing incorporation in the Commercial Registry Gazette within roughly 10 days. A tax officer then completes an onsite office check (yoklama) before active invoicing begins.
Pre-Incorporation Visit Checklist (With Your Licensed Counsel & SMMM):

items: Confirm legal structure (Ltd. Şti. vs. A.Ş.) and NACE activity codes with a licensed Turkish attorney.
Obtain apostilled corporate registry extracts and board resolutions if the parent is a foreign company.
Secure a compliant lease or virtual office contract in Istanbul before the Trade Registry filing.
Schedule in-person bank KYC meetings in Istanbul, as many Turkish banks require director attendance.
Coordinate your visit calendar alongside [Turkish business etiquette](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkish-business-etiquette) and local logistics.

body.text: What banking and work-permit rules apply after incorporation?

Owning shares in a Turkish company does not grant a foreign national the right to live or work in Türkiye. Corporate bank account opening requires strict in-person KYC verification, and foreign shareholder-managers who actively work in Türkiye must secure a Ministry of Labor work permit.

Per [Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/obtaining-a-work-permit.aspx) and [2026 shareholder criteria](https://halilbakirci.av.tr/en/foreign-shareholder-manager-work-permit-turkey-2026/), standard permits require five Turkish employees per foreign worker (starting month seven for a first shareholder permit), TRY 500,000 capital, and 20% foreign ownership—unless the shareholder invests USD 100,000 or more, waiving the five-employee rule. Confirm exemptions with licensed counsel.

faq.q: Can I register a Turkish company remotely without flying to Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes, via a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney issued to a licensed Turkish lawyer. However, most Turkish commercial banks still require an authorized signatory to visit a branch in person for corporate account KYC approval.

faq.q: Do I need a Turkish citizen as a partner or director?
faq.a: No. Foreigners can own 100% of the shares and serve as the sole director or board member of either an LLC or JSC, outside narrow regulated industries.

faq.q: Is a virtual office legal for company incorporation in Türkiye?
faq.a: Yes, for service, software, and consulting firms, provided a formal lease exists and a representative can meet the tax officer during the physical address inspection (yoklama).

faq.q: How much does an SMMM (certified public accountant) cost monthly?
faq.a: Monthly SMMM retainers vary by company type, transaction volume, and employee count, guided by TÜRMOB's annual minimum fee tariff. Request a written scope directly from a licensed SMMM.

faq.q: Does a JSC require a full-time retained lawyer in Türkiye?
faq.a: Under the Turkish Commercial Code, a Joint Stock Company with paid-in capital of at least five times the statutory minimum (currently TRY 1,250,000) must retain a contracted Turkish attorney.
